'''Warázu''', also known as '''Pauserna''' or '''Guarasugwé''' (Guarasú'we), is a moribund [[Tupi–Guaraní languages|Tupi–Guaraní language]] of [[Brazil]]. It was also formerly spoken in [[Bolivia]].<ref name="Ramirez 2017">{{Cite journal |last=Ramirez |first=Henri |last2=Vegini |first2=Valdir |last3=França |first3=Maria Cristina Victorino de |date=2017 |title=O warázu do Guaporé (tupi-guarani): Primeira descrição linguística |trans-title=Warázu of Guaporé (Tupi-Guarani): first linguistic description |journal=LIAMES |language=Portuguese |volume=17 |issue=2 |pages=411–506 |doi=10.20396/liames.v17i0.8647468 |doi-access=free}}</ref> It is spoken by the [[Guarasugwé people]], who were estimated to number 125 according to a census in 2012.<ref name="Censo 2012">{{Cite web |title=Censo de Población y Vivienda 2012 Bolivia Características de la Población |trans-title=Population and Housing Census 2012 Bolivia Characteristics of the Population |url=http://inecloud.ine.gob.bo/owncloud/index.php/s/w2ZCFwI7qJrwTwD/download |website=Instituto Nacional de Estadística, República de Bolivia |page=29 |language=Spanish |access-date=2020-04-01 |archive-date=2021-08-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210801173154/https://inecloud.ine.gob.bo/owncloud/index.php/s/w2ZCFwI7qJrwTwD/download |url-status=dead }}</ref> It was previously considered to be extinct, but 4 speakers were found in 2006; this number had decreased to 2 in 2017.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web | url=https://periodicos.sbu.unicamp.br/ojs/index.php/liames/article/view/8647468/pdf | title=O warázu do Guaporé (tupi-guarani):primeira descrição linguística | trans-title=The Warázu of Guaporé (Tupi-Guarani): first linguistic description | website=eriodicos.sbu.unicamp.br | language=pt}}</ref>

==Classification==
Warázu is most closely related to [[Sirionó language|Sirionó]] and [[Yuqui language|Yuki]] (Yuqui). Ramirez (2017) places the classification of Warázu in the Guaraní subgroup of the [[Tupi-Guarani languages]] as follows:<ref name="Ramirez 2017" />

{{tree list}}
*Guaraní subgroup
**[[Guaraní language|Guaraní]]
**[[Tupinambá language|Tupinambá]]
**[[Guarayu language|Guarayu]]
**Warázu-Sirionoid
***Sirionoid ([[Sirionó language|Sirionó]], [[Yuqui language|Yuqui]], etc.)
***'''Warázu'''
{{tree list/end}}

==Names==
Speakers are also known as Guaraiutá, Guaraju, Pauserna, Guarasugwe, or Warazúkwe [waɾaðúkwe].<ref name="Ramirez 2017" />

==Demographics==
Ramirez (2017) found only 2 remaining speakers of Warázu, an elderly couple consisting of Känä́tsɨ [kənə́tsɨ] (José Frei Leite) and Híwa (Ernestina Moreno). They were born in Riozinho (Urukuríti) in [[Rondônia]], Brazil, and moved back and forth between Brazil and Bolivia until finally settling in [[Pimenteiras do Oeste]], [[Rondônia]].<ref name="Ramirez 2017" /><ref>{{cite news |last=Mori |first=Leticia |date=4 March 2018 |title=O Brasil tem 190 línguas indígenas em perigo de extinção |url=https://www.bbc.com/portuguese/brasil-43010108 |work=BBC |location=São Paulo |lang=pt |access-date=2021-03-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=17 December 2018 |title=Pesquisa etnolinguística de docentes da UNIR é tema de reportagem da BBC |url=https://www.unir.br/index.php?pag=noticias&id=26395 |work=Universidade Federal de Rondônia |location= |lang=pt |access-date=2021-03-04}}</ref>

Traditionally, the Warázu people had lived in the following 7 villages along the banks of the [[Guaporé River]]. However, the Warázu language is no longer spoken in these localities.

*Riozinho (Urukurɨ́ti) (on the banks of the Riozinho River, a tributary of the Guaporé River), Brazil
*Acurizal, Brazil
*Campo Grande (on the banks of the [[Paragúa River]], a tributary of the Guaporé River), Bolivia
*Bella Vista, Bolivia
*Jangada, Bolivia
*Barranco Vermelho, Bolivia
*Flechas, Bolivia
